In children under 5 years of age, 3–4 cycles of seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) and amodiaquine (AQ) likely reduce the incidence of severe malaria by approximately 4 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% confidence interval [CI]: 8 fewer to 2 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with moderate certainty due to a serious risk of bias. 2. In children aged 5–9 years, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ likely reduce the incidence of severe malaria by approximately 11 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 16 fewer to 8 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in four randomized controlled trials, with high certainty. 3. In children under 10 years of age, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ likely reduce the incidence of severe malaria by approximately 8 more cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 4 fewer to 86 more). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in two randomized controlled trials, with moderate certainty due to serious imprecision. 4. In children under 5 years of age in moderate transmission settings, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ may increase the incidence of all-cause hospitalization by approximately 8 more cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 4 fewer to 86 more). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with moderate certainty due to serious imprecision. 5. In children under 5 years of age in high transmission settings, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ reduce the incidence of all-cause hospitalization by approximately 50 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 87 fewer to 29 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with high certainty. 6. In children under 5 years of age, the use of artesunate-amodiaquine (AS-AQ) reduces the incidence of all-cause hospitalization by approximately 23 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 48 fewer to 11 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in six randomized controlled trials, with high certainty. 7. In children under 5 years of age, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ may reduce all-cause mortality by approximately 8 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 10 fewer to 6 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in four randomized controlled trials, with low certainty due to serious inconsistency and imprecision. 8. In children under 5 years of age, 5–6 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ may have little or no effect on all-cause mortality, with a difference of approximately 2 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 1 fewer to 5 more). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with very low certainty due to serious imprecision and a very serious risk of bias. 9. In children aged 5–9 years, 5–6 cycles of SMC with AS-AQ likely have little or no effect on all-cause mortality, with a difference of approximately 18 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 7 fewer to 9 more). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with moderate certainty due to serious imprecision. 10. In children aged 5–9 years, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ may have little or no effect on all-cause mortality, with a difference of approximately 5 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 4 fewer to 2 more). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with low certainty due to serious risk of bias and imprecision. 11. In children aged 5–9 years, 5–6 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ may increase or decrease all-cause mortality, with a difference of approximately 0 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 0 fewer to 4 more). This conclusion is based on data from 2,000 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with very low certainty due to serious imprecision and a very serious risk of bias. 12. In children under 5 years of age, SMC likely reduces parasite prevalence by approximately 137 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 146 fewer to 126 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in nine randomized controlled trials, with moderate certainty due to serious inconsistency. 13. In children under 5 years of age, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ reduce parasite prevalence by approximately 114 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 121 fewer to 108 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in four randomized controlled trials, with high certainty. 14. In children under 5 years of age, 5–6 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ likely reduce parasite prevalence by approximately 86 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 109 fewer to 58 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in two randomized controlled trials, with moderate certainty due to serious inconsistency. 15. In children under 5 years of age, 3–4 cycles of SMC with AS-AQ likely reduce parasite prevalence by approximately 136 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 194 fewer to 62 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with moderate certainty due to serious risk of bias. 16. In children under 5 years of age, 5–6 cycles of SMC with AS-AQ reduce parasite prevalence by approximately 149 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 165 fewer to 125 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with high certainty. 17. This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with high certainty. 18. In children under 10 years of age, SMC with SP+AQ reduces parasite prevalence by approximately 60 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 70 fewer to 47 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in two randomized controlled trials, with high certainty. 19. In children under 10 years of age, 3–4 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ reduce parasite prevalence by approximately 13 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 16 fewer to 7 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with high certainty. 20. In children under 10 years of age, 5–6 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ reduce parasite prevalence by approximately 157 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 183 fewer to 112 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with high certainty. 21. This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in six randomized controlled trials, with moderate certainty due to serious inconsistency. 22. This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in three randomized controlled trials, with moderate certainty due to serious inconsistency. 23. This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in two randomized controlled trials, with high certainty. 24. In children aged 5–9 years, 5–6 cycles of SMC with SP+AQ reduce the prevalence of any anemia by approximately 143 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 228 fewer to 24 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in one randomized controlled trial, with high certainty. 25. In children under 5 years of age, SMC likely reduces the prevalence of moderate anemia slightly, with a difference of approximately 18 fewer cases per 1,000 children (95% CI: 27 fewer to 7 fewer). This conclusion is based on data from 200 participants in six randomized controlled trials, with moderate certainty due to serious inconsistency.
